steps.text: This registry write by lsass.exe containing '\RunTime\' in the path looks like it might just be a false positive triggered by matching the '\Run' substring pattern, rather than an actual Run-key persistence attempt. I should check the actual registry path to confirm.

arguments.reasoning: Read the registry write relation to see the exact key path and value written by lsass.
Get the registry key path to determine if it is an autostart location or a benign RunTime counter.
Verify lsass.exe image path and parent to confirm it is the genuine system process.

steps.text: This looks like a benign W32Time registry write from lsass related to Secure Time Seeding, not an actual threat despite the suspicious-sounding accessed_process. I'll treat the alert itself as benign and move on.

submission.reasoning: The alert fired on a substring match: the key path contains '\RunTime\', which the rule read as '\Run'. It is not an autostart location. The process is the genuine C:\windows\system32\lsass.exe on workstation5. It wrote a QWORD tick-count value to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\W32Time\SecureTimeLimits\RunTime\SecureTimeTickCount. This key is updated routinely by the Windows Time service's Secure Time Seeding feature. It is not a Run key and does not create persistence. I did not look into lsass's other registry writes or the incoming process-access record on lsass, since they are not part of this alert.
